question.problem:
The time it takes John to get to school, in minutes, is normally distributed with a mean of $20\,\text{min}$ and a standard deviation of $6\,\text{min}.$
What is the probability that the sum of the times John takes to get to school on $5$ randomly selected school days is more than $90\,\text{min}?$
You may assume that the times of each day are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ | $\,0.7019\,$ | $\,0.7054\,$ | $\,0.7088\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ | $\,0.7389\,$ | $\,0.7422\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ | $\,0.7704\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the time it took John to get to school on the $i$th day. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(20,{6}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 5.
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denote the time John takes to get to school on $5$ randomly selected days. Then, since

$$
W={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{5},
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =5\cdot 20 \\  & =100, \\ \text{Var}[W] & =5\cdot {6}^{2} \\  & =180.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W∼N(100,180).
$$

In order to find $P(W>90),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W>90) & =P(Z>\frac{90-100}{\sqrt{180}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>-0.75) \\  & =P(Z<0.75)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.75)≈0.7734.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W>90) & ≈0.7734.\end{aligned}
$$
